newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche first quarter sales race ahead, profit may lag.
newsitem.headline: Porsche first quarter sales race ahead, profit may lag.

text.p: Porsche AG said Tuesday that it made a quick start in the 1996-1997 fiscal year with sales of its renowned sports car surging 40 percent in the first quarter.

Chairman Wendelin Wiedeking, speaking at the company's annual press conference, said that sales between August and October, helped by strong demand in the United States, climbed to 822 million marks ($525 million) on unit turnover of 6,181, a 55 percent increase.
Much of the reason for the strong first-quarter result was a 90 percent increase in sales of the 911 model in North America.

The figures were the latest sign of a turnaround at Porsche, which last month announced a profit of 48.1 million marks ($30.7 million) -- its largest profit in six years and an increase from 2.1 million marks ($1.3 million) the year before.
The Porsche chairman, however, went to lengths to downplay expectations of continued rapid profit growth this year, speaking of providing "credible" forecasts which the company could safely meet.

He said that although sales this year are likely to climb to over three billion marks ($1.88 billion) from about 2.8 billion marks ($1.79 billion), profits would only be "at least as good as in the previous year."
Much of the reason for the reserved forecast stems from Porsche's first new model in nearly two decades -- the Boxster.

"My slightly reserved attitude in making this forecast is attributable in particular to the expenditure we will still be incurring in this business year on the start-up of the Boxster, ongoing investments in future projects and further expenditure on markets," Wiedeking said.
The Boxster, the only other model Porsche makes besides the 30-year-old 911, debuted in October to rave reviews from the motoring press and has enjoyed demand much stronger than Porsche had expected.
Wiedeking said the company is considering ways to slash delivery times from about one year currently.
